title: DCLab's engine on what real tables hold: columns with no value, classes of one row, more classes than holdout rows
request: Found while screening real OpenML tables for S7 ('more ability'): the engine crashed on two of the first three.
spec: Every table a person can upload runs through every stage, or is refused with a reason it can act on; no split already drawn changes.
plan: Reproduce each crash on its real table.
The smallest fix where the value goes wrong.
Prove each test fails on the old code.

decisions.decision: A column with no value on the fit rows is filled with 0.
decisions.why: Its median does not exist; the models' imputer and the detectors already turn such a column into 0, fit on the fit rows only.

decisions.decision: Single-row classes stratified with the commonest class; the outcome unchanged.
decisions.why: A stratified split refuses a class of one row; every other table must split exactly as before, which strata(y) returning y itself guarantees.

decisions.decision: More classes than holdout rows: a random split, said in the split's description.
decisions.why: No stratified split exists then; the alternative was a crash.

decisions.decision: One positive in a binary table still refused at the split, with sklearn's own message.
decisions.why: Pooling it would only move the failure into the model with a vaguer error.

change: dclab_rnd/expansion/runner.py (the selected_mi fill, the text recipe's medians), dclab_rnd/expansion/datasets.py (strata, strata_note, the plain split), dclab_rnd/studio/export.py (the notebook's split cell draws the same strata), tests/test_engine_real_tables.py.

findings.defect: A table with columns that have no value crashed the features stage.
findings.scenario: OpenML 2 (anneal, 898 rows): four columns 100% missing; ValueError: Input X contains NaN.
findings.cause: selected_mi's mutual information filled gaps with the column's median, which does not exist.
findings.fix: fillna(0.0) after the median fill; the text recipe's medians likewise.

findings.defect: A multiclass table with classes of one row could not be split.
findings.scenario: OpenML 7: 24 classes, five of a single row: 'The least populated class in y has only 1 member'.
findings.fix: strata(y): single-row classes drawn with the commonest; the outcome itself otherwise.

findings.defect: The exported notebook still stratified on the outcome and crashed on those tables.
findings.scenario: A project like OpenML 7 now runs; its notebook's split cell raised the old error.
findings.fix: The cell draws the engine's own strata, written into it.

findings.defect: A lone positive moved the failure into the model, with a vaguer error.
findings.scenario: 200 rows, one 'yes': the split passed and the solver failed on one class.
findings.cause: strata pooled the only positive into the negatives.
findings.fix: With fewer than two classes of two rows, strata returns the outcome and the split refuses at once.

findings.defect: The text recipe's fill was untested.
findings.cause: Both tests had no text column.
findings.fix: A text table with an empty number column.

findings.defect: The record did not say classes were pooled.
findings.scenario: 'stratified random N of M rows' with five classes pooled.
findings.fix: strata_note: pooled classes, or not stratified and why.

findings.defect: More classes than holdout rows crashed the split.
findings.scenario: 50 rows, 25 classes of two rows: test_size 10 under 25 classes.
findings.cause: A stratified split needs a row of every class on each side.
findings.fix: A random split, said in the description.

measurements.name: the two real tables, screened again
measurements.gate: affected tests only (the owner's daytime rule)
measurements.result: OpenML 2 screened in 13.6 s, OpenML 7 in 12.7 s; 85 tests in 8 files pass; no earlier split changes (strata returns the outcome itself whenever every class has two rows)
limits: the real-table screens will find more: every failure is kept with its reason

outcome: Tables with empty columns or rare classes run through the engine, and the notebook splits them the same way.
lessons: Screening real tables is a robustness test of the whole product: two of the first three crashed it.
risks: Other real-table crashes are still to be found by the screens.
